svg.text: A chat message: the browser, the chat's taia.ds flow, the agent's flow
in through a one-shot POST and the controller's put; out through send-event! and the open SSE stream

text.tspan: ;; agent events are patches pushed down the stream

svg.text: procs talk only through their ports: 6 conns

g.text: The chat is a taia.ds connected component: a flow (controller → view) and an SSE stream the page keeps open.
The agent is a core.async.flow of its own: ui, llm and tools, with the model outside it.
@post('/ds/nds/todomvc.todo-chat/c1/send_message') carries the chat's signals, the typed text among them,
into a flow of its own, built from the chat's controller and view.
The controller hands the message to the agent
SEND_MESSAGE → :sending-message: it stores the user's message and puts [:user-message-sent …] on the agent's in-chan.
The POST is answered with the chat (the message, the thinking dots, a stop button), and its flow stops.
Inside the agent: ui → llm → tools → llm
ui routes the message to llm; llm asks tools for the chat's history (load-chat-messages-fn) and gets back
:llm-complete-requested: the messages, the system instructions and the tool descriptions.
llm calls the model, and returns at once
li/complete! streams on the HTTP client's thread (gpt-5-mini); the step's own output is :llm-reply-requested
for the UI's thinking state. The proc is free for other turns while the model works.
The model asks for a tool
Every callback comes back through llm's own :from-completion in-port (callback-chan), and llm re-emits it:
:execute-tools to tools, which runs update_todos (buy milk is in the list now), then tool-applied to ui and tools-applied to llm.
The answer streams back, chunk by chunk
With the tool's output in the history, the model answers in text. Each chunk becomes a :partial-llm-reply-received:
llm sends it to ui, and ui puts it on the agent's out-chan, as it did with llm-reply-requested and tool-applied.
From the agent's out-chan into the chat's flow
agent-output-handler's go-loop takes every event off the out-chan: (ds/send-event! chat-id user-id "partial_llm_reply_received" {…}).
The chat has an open connection, so the event goes into that connection's flow: the same controller and view.
Pushed down the open SSE stream
A server event has no request, so the machine-level :on takes it in any state: agent-reply puts it in the ctx and
todo-chat renders it as effects. Nobody asked, so they go down the stream: the tool card, then the words as they stream.
The final reply closes the turn
llm-reply-received takes the same road and swaps the partial reply for the message. Its data-init POSTs completion_done,
and the controller goes back to :displayed: the messages reload and the input is enabled again.
Two flows, joined by two puts
In: the chat controller's (>! in-chan [:user-message-sent …]). Out: agent-output-handler's ds/send-event! into the chat's connection.
Neither flow knows the other's procs, and only llm ever talks to the model.
